text:
sara (support): heads-up — customer reported a spike of 504s hitting hosted /v1/generate around 17:25 UTC. they say p95 requests are timing out after 30s. sample req ids: req_Abc123, req_XyZ987. repro: send 6 concurrent long-sequence requests (seq_len ~ 6k) -> 504s.
sara (support): curl they used: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"input": "<long prompt>", "max_tokens": 6000}'`
raj (oncall): thanks, pulling traces + logs now. can you drop the exact timestamps (to the second) if the customer has them?
sara (support): they sent logs, first 504 at 2026-03-17T17:25:12Z, then a burst for ~90s. attaching quota/usage note: tenant acme-pay on hosted-prod.
ops-bot: Alert: hosted.gateway.queue_depth > 480 for pool hosted-prod at 2026-03-17T17:25:10Z.
raj (oncall): seeing the same in metrics — continuous-batcher backlog climbs quickly. `batcher.backlog_count` peaked ~2300, `gateway.queue_depth` hit 512 (cap). p95 enqueue-to-dequeue ~2.9s, p99 ~8.4s.
mike (eng-runtime): that backlog -> tail latencies. any KV-cache misses around then? continuous batching + cold KV could cause long enqueue stalls.
raj (oncall): traces show a lot of KV cache evictions, `kvcache.miss_rate` jumped 6x. many requests queued waiting on KV warmup.
ingrid (sre): also seeing disk-backed model variant thrash on a few workers — `model_variant_swap` events correlate with the window. Might be routing fallback to quantized variants causing kernel warmups.
mike (eng-runtime): can you paste a short trace snippet?
raj (oncall): paste: ```
TRACE req_Abc123 | enqueue=0.42s | wait-batch=1.9s | kvcache-miss | model-load=2.6s | service-total=30.12s -> 504
TRACE req_XyZ987 | enqueue=0.10s | wait-batch=0.6s | kvcache-hit | service-total=5.2s -> 200
```
sara (support): customer posted payloads were gzip-encoded, lots of large prompts back-to-back. they said earlier they increased concurrency to compensate for higher latency.
mike (eng-runtime): gzip or large payloads increase memory pressure on batchers which can amplify eviction churn. combined with continuous batching, prefix caches get invalidated and we see a snowballing enqueue wait.
ingrid (sre): for an immediate mitigation I recommend: 1) temporarily raise `gateway.queue_depth` soft-limit for acme-pay to 800; 2) enable canary fallback to smaller quantized model variant for requests beyond 1s enqueue wait; 3) throttle tenant concurrency to 4.
raj (oncall): I can push a tenant-level throttle and toggle the model-fallback policy. rolling now: `rbacctl set-tenant-limit acme-pay concurrency=4`
ops-bot: action: tenant-limit updated for acme-pay by raj at 2026-03-17T17:28:02Z.
raj (oncall): toggled fallback policy to model-small-quantized for enqueues > 1s. watch metrics.
mike (eng-runtime): i'll open a runtime ticket to investigate kvcache eviction algorithm — hypothesis: huge gzipped prompts cause memory spike -> global eviction -> cascade. adding an experiment to prefer sticky KV warming for active tenants.
sara (support): customer confirmed errors reduced after throttling, still seeing occasional p95 blips. they want a root cause and change plan.
ingrid (sre): follow-ups: collect full heap profiles from impacted batchers, capture kvcache state, and add a short-lived circuit-breaker to reject requests that would exceed soft queue depth instead of letting them pile and trigger 30s gateway timeouts.
mike (eng-runtime): created ticket RUNTIME-5678 with initial triage notes + trace links: https://internal.redwood/oss/traces/RUNTIME-5678
raj (oncall): escalation summary for ops: - incident window 2026-03-17T17:25:10Z - 17:27:40Z - root-cause likely kvcache eviction + model-variant warmup + queue cap - mitigations applied: tenant throttle, fallback model, increased soft depth - next actions: runtime ticket, SRE add circuit-breaker, Prod eng kvcache change
sara (support): sending customer an update now w/ steps and ETA for deeper fix. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: follow-up check scheduled at 2026-03-18T09:00:00Z by ingrid.
raj (oncall): marking incident as mitigated for now, tracking in #postmortems once we have RCA. anyone taking ownership of postmortem?
mike (eng-runtime): i'll own the postmortem + link to RUNTIME-5678.
sara (support): thanks all — will keep customer posted and close the support ticket when postmortem is available.
